sop_modules.name: Exterior Engineered Wood Siding Protection & Equipment Setup
sop_modules.description: Deploy landscape/hardscape protection, mask fixtures, set up access equipment and spray rigs. Window/door protection is NOT this spec's responsibility — belongs in window/door specs (wood siding RC-001).

tasks.name: Landscape Protection Setup
tasks.description: Deploy tarps and plastic sheeting along house perimeter where landscape is adjacent to siding work area. Measured in linear feet along the foundation/siding line. Full cover for spray/spray_backroll, edge tarps for brush/roll.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage of plantings within spray drift zone (10-15 ft for airless). Secure tarps against wind with stakes or weights.

tasks.name: Hardscape Protection Setup
tasks.description: Deploy drop cloths and plastic over walkways, patios, and driveways adjacent to siding.

quality_notes.all: Tape plastic to foundation at grade line. Extend coverage to drip/overspray zone. Canvas for crew traffic areas.

tasks.name: Fixture and Utility Masking
tasks.description: Mask exterior light fixtures, house numbers, utility panels, hose bibs. Bag and tape HVAC units if adjacent.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage of all fixtures and utility connections on working elevation. Do not block HVAC intake/exhaust if unit is running.

tasks.name: Spray Equipment Setup
tasks.description: Set up ladders, scaffold, or lift per access_type. Configure airless sprayer with 517 tip, 60-mesh filter, hoses. Stage materials for LP SmartSide engineered wood siding.

quality_notes.all: Verify tip size: 515-517 for all profiles. 60-mesh black filter for latex. Stage enough material for full elevation run. For spray_backroll: stage roller frame + 18-inch covers alongside sprayer.

tasks.name: Brush/Roll Equipment Setup
tasks.description: Set up ladders, scaffold, or lift per access_type. Stage brushes, rollers, trays, and materials.

quality_notes.all: Stage enough material for full elevation run. Extension poles for elevated work.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Landscape/hardscape protection first → Fixture masking → Equipment setup last.

sop_modules.name: Engineered Wood Siding Surface Preparation
sop_modules.description: NC engineered wood prep: low-pressure wash (NO power washing — damages factory primer, forces water into OSB core), scuff sand for adhesion, end-seal ALL cut edges (most critical prep task — prevents irreversible OSB springback), caulk siding-to-trim joints (NOT butt joints), dust cleanup, moisture check.

tasks.name: Low-Pressure Wash
tasks.description: Clean siding surface with garden hose and soft-to-medium bristle brush. Remove construction dust, dirt, and debris. HIGH-PRESSURE POWER WASHING IS PROHIBITED on engineered wood — damages factory primer, forces water into OSB core at joints and cut edges, causes irreversible swelling.

quality_notes.QT3: Full low-pressure wash. Allow 24 hr dry time. Verify MC < 15% before proceeding.
quality_notes.QT4: Full low-pressure wash with TSP solution. Allow 24-48 hr dry time. Moisture meter check mandatory.

tasks.name: Scuff Sand for Adhesion
tasks.description: Light scuff sand siding surface with 150-180 grit for mechanical adhesion profile. Required for factory-primed and factory-finished surfaces. Creates tooth for primer/paint bond.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Full surface scuff sand — critical for bonding primer adhesion on oven-baked ExpertFinish
Bare engineered wood has sufficient tooth

quality_notes.QT3: Light scuff. Not removing material — creating tooth.
quality_notes.QT4: Full surface scuff. Uniform scratch pattern. Inspect for missed areas.

tasks.name: End-Seal Field-Cut Edges
tasks.description: Brush LP SmartSide Cut End Seal on ALL field-cut edges. Cut edges expose OSB core that absorbs water — the #1 failure mode for engineered wood (FM-001). Unsealed edges cause irreversible thickness swell (springback) due to MDI resin bond failure. Includes butt joints, miters, and field cuts.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Factory primer covers face but cut edges are bare OSB
Factory finish covers face but cut edges remain unsealed
Assumed sealed during prior prime application

quality_notes.all: EVERY cut edge sealed. Non-negotiable for LP SmartSide warranty and performance. Inspect all joints, miters, and field cuts. Use LP SmartSide Cut End Seal (CON_ENSD_END_SEALER) — NOT generic wood sealer.

tasks.name: Caulk Siding-to-Trim Joints
tasks.description: Apply exterior paintable caulk to all siding-to-trim joints (siding-to-corner boards, siding-to-window casings, siding-to-door casings). Do NOT caulk field butt joints — creates moisture trap behind the joint, trapping water against OSB core (per research RF-012). Use flexible caulk (polyurethane or siliconized acrylic).

quality_notes.QT3: All siding-to-trim joints caulked. Smooth tool.
quality_notes.QT4: All joints caulked with consistent bead. Precision tool smooth. Inspect for uniformity.

tasks.name: Moisture Content Verification
tasks.description: Check moisture content of engineered wood siding with pin-type moisture meter. Must read < 15% MC before any coating application. Check at cut ends, joints, and low elevations where water collects. Engineered wood retains moisture longer at joints and cut ends than fiber cement.

quality_notes.QT3: Check all cut ends, joints, and low-elevation areas.
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic check with documented readings. All areas must pass < 15% MC.

tasks.name: Prep Dust Cleanup
tasks.description: Remove sanding dust and debris from all surfaces before coating. Tack cloth or compressed air.

quality_notes.all: All dust removed. Surface ready for primer application.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Low-pressure wash → Dry time (24-48 hr, MC < 15%) → Scuff sand (factory-primed/factory-finished) → End-seal ALL cut edges → Caulk siding-to-trim joints → Moisture check → Dust cleanup.

sop_modules.name: Engineered Wood Siding Field Prime Coat
sop_modules.description: Full field prime coat. Two substrate-driven primer paths: (1) standard acrylic primer for factory-primed and bare wood (SYS_EXT_EW_PRIMER_ACRYLIC), (2) bonding primer for factory-finished ExpertFinish (SYS_EXT_EW_PRIMER_BONDING). NO alkali-resistant primer path — engineered wood is wood-based (neutral pH), NOT cementitious. Skipped entirely for SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD. spray_backroll valid for textured profiles and T1-11.

tasks.name: Prime Coat — Spray Application
tasks.description: Apply full prime coat by airless spray. Even, consistent mil thickness across all siding field. Primer product determined by substrate state: acrylic primer (SYS_EXT_EW_PRIMER_ACRYLIC) for factory-primed/bare wood, bonding primer (SYS_EXT_EW_PRIMER_BONDING) for factory-finished ExpertFinish.

quality_notes.QT2: Even coverage. No holidays or thin spots.
quality_notes.QT3: Uniform mil build. Inspect for coverage.
quality_notes.QT4: Perfect uniformity. Inspect under raking light at 3 ft.

tasks.name: Prime Coat — Spray + Back-Roll Application
tasks.description: Apply full prime coat by airless spray followed immediately by back-rolling with 18-inch roller. Back-rolling distributes primer into T1-11 vertical grooves and textured profiles (cedarmill, roughsawn). MANDATORY for T1-11 profile. Two-person operation: sprayer leads, roller follows while coating is wet.

quality_notes.all: Back-roll IMMEDIATELY while primer is wet. Roller must follow sprayer within 30-60 seconds. Even roller distribution into all grooves. No dry spots in T1-11 channels.

tasks.name: Prime Coat — Brush/Roll Application
tasks.description: Apply full prime coat by brush and roller. Brush for edges and transitions, roller for open field. Primer product determined by substrate state.

quality_notes.all: Even coverage. Work primer into surface texture. No holidays. Maintain wet edge.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Single prime coat. Method by application_method dimension. Substrate state determines primer product (acrylic vs bonding). Module SKIPPED entirely when substrate_state = SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD. spray_backroll adds roller step for T1-11 and textured profiles.

sop_modules.name: Engineered Wood Siding Finish Coat 1
sop_modules.description: First finish coat. Three application method paths: spray-only (smooth profiles), spray + back-roll (T1-11 and textured profiles — MANDATORY for T1-11), brush/roll (fallback for <750 SF, occupied adjacent, or high wind). KEY DIFFERENCE from fiber cement: back-rolling IS valid and required for grooved/textured engineered wood.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 1 — Spray Application
tasks.description: Apply first finish coat by airless spray. For smooth LP SmartSide lap and panel profiles. Consistent mil build, uniform coverage.

quality_notes.QT2: Even coverage. No drips or holidays.
quality_notes.QT3: Uniform mil build. No visible spray pattern at 6 ft.
quality_notes.QT4: Uniform mil build. No visible pattern at 3 ft. LP SmartSide-approved product required.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 1 — Spray + Back-Roll Application
tasks.description: Apply first finish coat by airless spray followed immediately by back-rolling with 18-inch roller. MANDATORY for T1-11 profile — deep vertical grooves require roller to distribute coating. Recommended for cedarmill and roughsawn textures. Two-person operation: sprayer leads, roller follows while coating is wet.

quality_notes.QT2: Even coverage. Roller distributes paint into all grooves.
quality_notes.QT3: Uniform distribution. No dry spots in T1-11 channels. Roller follows sprayer within 30-60 seconds.
quality_notes.QT4: Perfect groove coverage. Inspect all vertical channels at 3 ft. Consistent mil build across face and groove surfaces.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 1 — Brush/Roll Application
tasks.description: Apply first finish coat by brush and roller. Fallback method for small projects <750 SF, occupied adjacent areas, or high wind conditions.

quality_notes.all: Even coverage. Consistent roller texture. Maintain wet edge to lap line.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: First finish coat. Spray-only for smooth profiles, spray+backroll for T1-11/textured, brush/roll as fallback. Allow recoat time per product TDS before interstage/coat 2. QT2 may stop here (single finish coat).

sop_modules.name: Engineered Wood Siding Interstage Inspection
sop_modules.description: Inspect first finish coat, touch up defects. Light sand at QT4 only (220 grit). Module skipped for QT2 single-coat systems.

tasks.name: Interstage Inspection
tasks.description: Inspect first finish coat for holidays, runs, sags, and coverage defects. For spray_backroll method: also check T1-11 grooves for dry spots and uneven distribution.

quality_notes.QT3: Quick scan for obvious defects — runs, sags, holidays. Check T1-11 grooves if applicable.
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic inspection at 6 ft viewing distance. Mark all visible defects. Raking light inspection on visible elevations.

tasks.name: Interstage Light Sand
tasks.description: Light sand between finish coats with 220 grit for mechanical adhesion and leveling. QT4 only — not required at QT3.

quality_notes.QT4: Light scuff sand. Remove nibs and defects. Uniform scratch pattern. Do not sand through primer or first coat.

tasks.name: Interstage Touch-Up
tasks.description: Repair defects found during interstage inspection. Brush touch-up.

quality_notes.QT4: Fix all defects found during inspection. Blend repairs into surrounding finish.

tasks.name: Intercoat Dust Removal
tasks.description: Remove sanding dust before second coat. Tack cloth or compressed air.

quality_notes.all: All sanding dust removed before second finish coat.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect → Sand (QT4 only) → Touch up → Dust removal → Coat 2. Module skipped for QT2 single-coat systems.
sop_modules.run_rule: Runs after finish coat 1, before finish coat 2. Skipped for QT2 single-coat.

sop_modules.name: Engineered Wood Siding Finish Coat 2
sop_modules.description: Second (final) finish coat. Required at QT3 and QT4. Skipped at QT2 (single coat). Three application method paths matching coat 1 — spray, spray+backroll, or brush/roll.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 2 — Spray Application
tasks.description: Apply second (final) finish coat by airless spray. Critical for appearance and film build. Smooth profiles only.

quality_notes.QT3: Even coverage. Consistent appearance. No visible pattern at 6 ft.
quality_notes.QT4: Uniform mil build. No visible pattern at 3 ft. Final appearance coat.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 2 — Spray + Back-Roll Application
tasks.description: Apply second (final) finish coat by airless spray followed by back-rolling. Same method as coat 1 — consistent texture on T1-11 and textured profiles. Two-person operation.

quality_notes.QT3: Even distribution in all grooves. Consistent appearance.
quality_notes.QT4: Perfect coverage. Every groove filled. Inspect at 3 ft. Final appearance coat.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 2 — Brush/Roll Application
tasks.description: Apply second finish coat by brush and roller. Fallback method. Final coat.

quality_notes.all: Even coverage. No brush marks. Maintain wet edge to lap line. Final coat.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Second and final finish coat. Same application method as coat 1. Skipped at QT2.

sop_modules.name: Engineered Wood Siding Final Inspection
sop_modules.description: Final walkthrough of completed siding finish. Inspect all elevations. Touch up defects found.

tasks.name: Final Walkthrough Inspection
tasks.description: Walk all elevations and inspect finished siding for coverage, consistency, and defects. For spray_backroll method: verify uniform appearance and consistent groove coverage on T1-11.

quality_notes.QT2: Ground-level walkthrough. Quick scan for misses.
quality_notes.QT3: Ground-level walkthrough at 6-10 ft viewing distance. Check all elevations.
quality_notes.QT4: Ground-level with binoculars for upper elevations. 6 ft viewing standard. Raking light check on primary elevations.

tasks.name: Final Touch-Up
tasks.description: Brush touch-up of defects found during final inspection.

quality_notes.QT4: Fix every defect. Blend seamlessly at 3 ft standard.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect all elevations → Touch up → Sign off.

sop_modules.name: Engineered Wood Siding Cleanup & Protection Teardown
sop_modules.description: Remove all protection materials, clean equipment, restore site.

tasks.name: Protection Material Removal
tasks.description: Remove all masking tape, landscape tarps, hardscape covers, fixture bags, HVAC covers.

quality_notes.all: Check for tape residue. Remove all protection materials completely. Inspect landscape for overspray.

tasks.name: Clean Equipment
tasks.description: Flush airless sprayer, clean tips and filters, coil hoses. Clean brushes and rollers if used. For spray_backroll: clean roller frames and dispose of saturated roller covers.

quality_notes.all: Full flush cycle for sprayer. Tips and filters cleaned and stored. Roller covers disposed of properly.

tasks.name: Site Debris Cleanup
tasks.description: Collect all debris — sandpaper, caulk tubes, tape, sealer containers, paint cans, used roller covers. Leave site clean.

quality_notes.all: Site restored to pre-work condition. All materials and debris removed.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Protection teardown → Equipment cleaning → Site cleanup.

round_configurations.name: Prime + 2 Finish Coats
round_configurations.description: Standard NC sequence: 1 field prime + 2 finish coats. Required at QT3/QT4.
round_configurations.notes: LP SmartSide warranty requires minimum 2 topcoats. Field prime over factory prime is mandatory per LP warranty even on factory-primed boards.

round_configurations.name: Prime + 1 Finish Coat (Economy)
round_configurations.description: Economy QT2 sequence: 1 field prime + 1 finish coat.
round_configurations.notes: QT2 economy tier. Single finish coat acceptable on primed surfaces. LP warranty requires minimum 2 coats but QT2 accepts the trade-off.

round_configurations.name: 2 Finish Coats Only (Field-Primed)
round_configurations.description: Skip prime, direct to 2 finish coats. For SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD only.
round_configurations.notes: Field prime already applied in prior mobilization.

round_configurations.name: 1 Finish Coat Only (Economy, Field-Primed)
round_configurations.description: Economy single finish coat on field-primed surface.
round_configurations.notes: QT2 economy on already-primed surface. Minimum viable scope.

key_differences_from_fiber_cement: Back-roll tasks added: TSK_ENSD_PRIME_SPRAY_BACKROLL, TSK_ENSD_FINISH_1_SPRAY_BACKROLL, TSK_ENSD_FINISH_2_SPRAY_BACKROLL — fiber cement has NO back-roll tasks
Only 2 primer paths (acrylic + bonding) — fiber cement has 3 (acrylic + alkali-resistant + bonding)
Application method dimension includes spray_backroll — fiber cement only has spray and brush_roll
Edge sealer is LP SmartSide-specific OSB sealer (CON_ENSD_END_SEALER) — fiber cement uses cementitious edge sealer
Moisture check task added (TSK_ENSD_MOISTURE_CHECK) — engineered wood is more moisture-sensitive than fiber cement
No SS_EXT_BARE_FIBERCEMENT state — uses SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD instead
T1-11 profile mandates spray_backroll via applies_when on siding_profile dimension

assumptions.value: spray_backroll application method is MANDATORY for T1-11 profile
assumptions.source: Exterior_Application_Methods_Doctrine.md Part A §6: 'T-1-11 and rough-sawn siding: Deep vertical grooves need roller to distribute paint' — listed under Mandatory Back-Rolling
assumptions.note: Explicit doctrine: T1-11 requires back-rolling. spray_backroll tasks gate on application_method dimension. Engine enforces T1-11 → spray_backroll constraint.

assumptions.value: Low-pressure wash (garden hose + soft brush) only — power washing prohibited
assumptions.source: Exterior_Engineered_Wood_Fiber_Cement_Doctrine.md §3: 'High-pressure power washing: Strips paint films, damages surface texture, forces water behind wall assembly'
assumptions.note: Explicit doctrine prohibition applies to both fiber cement and engineered wood.

assumptions.value: End-cut edge sealing is non-negotiable for all field-cut engineered wood edges
assumptions.source: Exterior_Engineered_Wood_Fiber_Cement_Doctrine.md §6-7: 'Seal, prime, and paint ALL field-cut edges to prevent water intrusion'
assumptions.note: Edge wicking into OSB core causes irreversible springback — the #1 failure mode.

assumptions.value: No alkali-resistant primer path — engineered wood is wood-based (neutral pH), NOT cementitious
assumptions.source: Exterior_Engineered_Wood_Fiber_Cement_Doctrine.md §4: alkali-resistant primer specified for 'bare fiber cement (pH 13)' only
assumptions.note: Engineered wood composition is wood strands + resin, not cement. Standard acrylic primer is correct for all non-factory-finished states.

assumptions.value: Do NOT caulk field butt joints on engineered wood siding — creates moisture trap
assumptions.source: Research RF-012, confirmed by Exterior_Engineered_Wood_Fiber_Cement_Doctrine.md §7: 'Manufacturers recommend joint flashing (slipsheets) behind joints rather than relying on caulk'
assumptions.note: Caulk at butt joints traps moisture against OSB core. Siding-to-trim joints ONLY.

assumptions.value: Moisture check task added for engineered wood — more moisture-sensitive than fiber cement
assumptions.source: Exterior_Engineered_Wood_Fiber_Cement_Doctrine.md §3: 'Wood substrates must dry to MC < 15% before painting'
assumptions.note: MC check is mandatory per doctrine. Fiber cement sibling does not have explicit moisture check task — fiber cement is less moisture-retentive.

assumptions.value: spray_backroll requires two-person crew (sprayer + roller operator)
assumptions.source: Exterior_Application_Methods_Doctrine.md Part A §6 and Part B §8: 'Requires 2-person crew; coordination critical'
assumptions.note: Production rate impact: spray_backroll is slower than spray-only (~150-200 SF/hr vs 300-500 SF/hr). Estimation Engineer must account for two-person crew in rate calculations.
